learn.title: Geothermal Energy: Earth's Hidden Heat
learn.intro: Harnessing Earth's internal heat provides a stable, 24/7 renewable energy source, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and cutting carbon emissions by up to 99% compared to coal.
learn.c1_text: Geothermal plants tap underground reservoirs via wells, converting steam or hot water into electricity. The U.S. generates 3.7 GW from geothermal, enough to power 2.6 million homes annually.
learn.c2_text: Binary cycle plants use heat exchangers to vaporize a secondary fluid, avoiding direct contact with reservoirs. This method enables use in lower-temperature regions, expanding geothermal potential globally.
learn.c3_text: India's Parvati Valley hosts Asia's first closed-loop plant (15 MW), demonstrating scalability. The government aims for 5 GW by 2030 under the National Geothermal Mission.
learn.stat4: Emissions: 99% lower than coal per kWh

learn.title: Flow Batteries: Grid-Scale Energy Storage
learn.intro: Flow batteries store renewable energy efficiently for hours, balancing grid demand and enabling 100% clean energy systems.
learn.c1_text: Vanadium flow batteries use liquid electrolytes in tanks, decoupling power (stacks) and energy (tank size). A 200 MWh system in China stores energy for 10+ hours.
learn.c2_text: Iron flow batteries reduce costs by 70% vs. vanadium, using abundant materials. A 2023 pilot in Germany achieved 90% efficiency, ideal for solar/wind integration.
learn.c3_text: India's 280 GW renewable target by 2030 requires storage. The 2022 National Energy Storage Mission prioritizes flow batteries for solar farms.

learn.title: Grid Balancing: Real-Time Energy Dance
learn.intro: Grid operators balance electricity supply and demand every second, ensuring lights stay on even as renewables fluctuate.
learn.c1_text: Grid frequency (50 Hz in India) must stay stable. A 1% frequency drop triggers automated responses, like reducing wind output or activating hydro reserves.
learn.c2_text: Smart grids incentivize users to shift usage (e.g., AC during off-peak hours). In California, such programs reduced peak demand by 4% in 2022.
learn.c3_text: India's grid faces 30% renewable integration by 2030. The 2023 National Grid Integration Plan mandates 25 GW of flexible resources like batteries.
learn.stat3: Battery response time: <4 ms vs. coal: 15 min

learn.title: Capacity Factor: Power vs. Reality
learn.intro: Capacity factor reveals how much energy a plant actually produces versus its maximum potential.
learn.c1_text: Capacity factor = Actual output / (Max capacity × Hours). A 500 MW solar plant with 25% CF produces 1,095 GWh/year (500 × 24 × 0.25).
learn.c2_text: Geothermal (90% CF) outperforms wind (35% CF) due to constant heat. India's Kamataka plant operates at 92% CF, vs. Jaisalmer solar at 28%.
learn.c3_text: India's average solar CF is 25%, but Gujarat's Bhadla plant reaches 35%. Low CF requires oversizing solar farms to meet targets.
learn.stat4: Cost impact: 35% CF doubles solar LCOE vs. 25%

learn.title: Floating Offshore Wind: Deep-Water Tech
learn.intro: Floating platforms unlock wind energy in 80% of global oceans, where fixed turbines can't reach.
learn.c1_text: Spar buoys (e.g., Hywind Scotland) use anchors to stabilize 150-meter turbines. They generate 21 MW in Scotland's rough seas, withstanding 100-year storms.
learn.c2_text: Floating wind costs dropped 45% since 2010. South Korea's 7 MW pilot uses semi-submersibles, targeting 10 GW by 2030.
learn.c3_text: India's 7,000 GW offshore potential includes floating tech for Andaman Sea. The 2023 National Wind Energy Mission prioritizes floating for deep-water zones.

learn.title: Electric Vehicles: Powering the Future
learn.intro: EVs convert 77% of grid energy to motion, vs. 12-30% for gasoline cars, slashing emissions and oil dependence.
learn.c1_text: Lithium-ion batteries store 250 Wh/kg. A Tesla Model 3 uses 1,000 lbs of battery material, providing 358 miles of range (2023 model).
learn.c2_text: Regenerative braking recovers 15-25% of energy during deceleration. In stop-and-go traffic, this can extend range by 10-15% (e.g., Nissan Leaf).
learn.c3_text: India's EV market grew 140% in 2023, with 2.5 million sales. The 2022 FAME II policy targets 30% EV penetration by 2030, supported by 500+ charging stations.
learn.stat4: EV emissions: 50% lower than ICE cars (India grid)
